paper_a.title: A New Proof of Szemeredi's Theorem

metadata.description: Gowers (2001) is the eventual quantitative resolution of the line of inquiry opened by Erdos-Turan (1936). Erdos-Turan introduce $r(N)$, prove the linear bound $r(2N)\le N$ and the density bound $r(N)<(1/2+\epsilon)N$, conjecture $r(N)=o(N)$, and pose the analogous question for $l$-term APs. Gowers proves a fully quantitative version of Szemeredi's theorem covering all $k$, which strictly extends every density question raised in the 1936 paper, via higher-order Fourier analysis (Gowers norms) — a wholly new technical apparatus far beyond the elementary case-analysis used in 1936. This is a textbook EXT relationship: same fundamental object, generalized to all $k$ with explicit (tower-type) bounds. Both extractions are PDF-fallback so we lean on names/types over LaTeX-string matching.

matches.explanation: Erdos-Turan's open conjecture 'it is probable that $r(N)=o(N)$' is the original 3-AP density conjecture. Gowers's Main Theorem (TP339.13) settles the strong (quantitative) form for all $k$: $|A|\ge\delta N$ implies a $k$-AP for $N$ above a tower bound. So Gowers's theorem includes — quantitatively, with explicit bounds, and for every $k\ge 3$ — exactly the conjecture Erdos and Turan stated for $k=3$. Analogous rather than exact: the conjecture is qualitative ($o(N)$), Gowers proves a much stronger quantitative version.

TP339.4 is the $k=3$ case (Roth's theorem) re-proved by Gowers as the warm-up. This is exactly the resolution of Erdos-Turan's $r(N)=o(N)$ conjecture for 3-APs (proved by Roth 1953; the Erdos-Turan paper is the source of that conjecture). Same statement at $k=3$, in present-day language.

Szemeredi's theorem (cited by Gowers as TP339.2) is the qualitative form of the general-$k$ generalization of $r(N)=o(N)$. Erdos-Turan introduce both the $k=3$ conjecture (OpenP340.1) and its general-$l$ extension via $r_l(N)$ (DP340.3); Szemeredi's theorem is precisely the assertion that $r_l(N) = o(N)$ for every $l$, which Erdos-Turan implicitly conjectured by introducing $r_l$. Many-to-one because Szemeredi covers both questions at once.

Both papers cite van der Waerden's theorem and the function $f(k,l)$ verbatim. TP339.1 in Gowers and TP340.3 in Erdos-Turan are the same external statement (van der Waerden 1927); DP340.4 is Erdos-Turan's definition of the same $f(k,l)$. Both papers carry it as cited-external context.

Both are quantitative bounds on the van der Waerden number $f(k,l)$. Erdos-Turan derive $f(k,l)<l^{e^{k\log k}}$ (or similar) CONDITIONAL on the Szekeres conjecture (CnjP340.2). Gowers's CP339.25 is the UNCONDITIONAL tower-of-twos bound (resolving Graham's conjecture for $k\ge 9$). Same target — quantitative van der Waerden — at vastly different strengths and one conditional vs unconditional.

Erdos-Turan's CP340.1 says the Szekeres conjecture would imply infinitely many $k$-APs of primes. Gowers cites Erdos's stronger conjecture (OpenP339.1): every set with divergent reciprocal sum contains arbitrarily long APs (which the primes satisfy). Both are statements about $k$-APs in the primes, at successive strengthenings: Erdos-Turan's is conditional on Szekeres; Erdos's general form (cited by Gowers) is unconditional but open. Analogous: same target, different framings.

Both are quantitative density bounds for AP-free sets. Erdos-Turan's Theorem II (TP340.2) gives $r(N)<(1/2+\epsilon)N$ for large $N$ — i.e. density strictly below $1/2$ for 3-AP-free. Gowers's quantitative main theorem (TP339.3) gives $|A|\ge N(\log\log N)^{-c(k)}$ implies a $k$-AP — a vastly stronger sub-constant density bound, for all $k$. Same role (quantitative density theorem), enormous gap in strength.

Erdos-Turan Theorem I (TP340.1) is the very first non-trivial upper bound on $r$: $r(2N)\le N$ for $N\ge 8$. It plays the historical role of being the first density theorem in the line that Gowers ultimately closes with the tower-bound main theorem. Conceptually analogous (both are upper bounds on the density of 3-AP-free / $k$-AP-free sets); enormous quantitative gap; included to mark Erdos-Turan TP340.1 as the historical seed of TP339.13.

Tenuous but defensible: Erdos-Turan's ternary-digit construction (ExP340.2) builds 3-AP-free sets via sums of $\{0,1\}$-valued digit indicators in base $3$ — i.e. integers of the form $u+1$ where $u$ has only ternary digits in $\{0,1\}$. This is essentially a $\{0,1\}^d$-cube embedded in $\mathbb{Z}$, the same combinatorial object Gowers formalises as the '$d$-dimensional cube' (DP339.7) underlying Gowers norms. Low confidence because Gowers's cubes are the affine target object inside $A$ (positive structure), while Erdos-Turan use them to BUILD a 3-AP-FREE set (negative structure); the formal correspondence is suggestive rather than literal.

Both papers state conjectures about the exact AP-count or the exact maximal AP-free density — the 'inverse / sharpness' direction. Szekeres (cited by Erdos-Turan) conjectures the ternary construction is optimal; Gowers's CnjP339.2 conjectures the precise expected AP-count for higher-degree-uniform sets. Both are 'sharp lower-bound' open problems on the structure side of Szemeredi's theorem; very different formulations, so analogous and medium confidence.

Erdos-Turan's 'A-sequence belonging to $N$' (a 3-AP-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$) is the core defined object of the 1936 paper. Gowers does not introduce a named Level-1 definition for this object — he works with $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_N$ of density $\delta$ and asks for any AP, never naming the AP-free condition. Treated as a paper-original Erdos-Turan node with no direct Gowers Level-1 counterpart.

Erdos-Turan's $r(N)$ is the central function of the 1936 paper. Gowers does not name or use this extremal function as a Level-1 definition; he works directly with subsets of given density. The role $r(N)$ plays (extremal AP-free size) is implicit throughout Gowers but not extracted as a definition node, so this Erdos-Turan paper-original node has no Gowers Level-1 counterpart.

Erdos-Turan's reflection symmetry of A-sequences is a tiny ad-hoc lemma used only inside the case analysis for small $N$. No counterpart in Gowers, whose techniques operate at the asymptotic / harmonic-analytic level.
Translation invariance of A-sequences: trivial elementary observation in Erdos-Turan, used only for small-$N$ casework. No Level-1 counterpart in Gowers.

Subadditivity of $r$: a one-line elementary lemma central to Erdos-Turan's induction. Gowers does not use this kind of subadditivity argument anywhere; his density-increment iteration is the modern replacement, but it operates on $A$ via Fourier coefficients, not on the extremal function $r$. No counterpart.
Tabulated small-$N$ values of $r$: pure base-case computation in Erdos-Turan. No analogue in Gowers.

Proof of Theorem I via finite induction with subadditivity: technique not used anywhere in Gowers. The Erdos-Turan proof structure (small-base-case + subadditive induction) is fundamentally different from Gowers's density-increment iteration via higher-order Fourier analysis.

Proof of Theorem II via doubling-style induction on tabulated values: again, fundamentally elementary. Gowers's analogue (proof of TP339.13) uses Gowers norms, density-increment, and a multi-section structural theorem; nothing in common at the proof level. Listed as 'none' because PP340.2 is a paper-original Level-1 node.
Discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{Z}_N$ — the fundamental tool of modern additive combinatorics. Erdos-Turan 1936 predates Fourier-analytic methods in this area; no counterpart.
Convolution (non-standard form). Tool from modern additive combinatorics; no counterpart in Erdos-Turan.
Balanced function $f_A$. Modern Fourier-analytic device; no counterpart in Erdos-Turan.
$\alpha$-uniformity (linear/Gowers $U^2$ flavour). The defining technical input to Gowers's argument. No counterpart in Erdos-Turan, who have no notion of pseudorandomness.
Iterated difference function and $\alpha$-uniformity of degree $d$ (Gowers $U^{d+1}$ norm prerequisites). The central novel objects of the paper; no counterpart in 1936.
$\gamma$-additive function (additive-quadruple counting). Modern Freiman/Balog-Szemeredi-language object; no Erdos-Turan counterpart.
Freiman homomorphism of order $k$. Object from Freiman 1966 and later additive combinatorics; postdates Erdos-Turan.
Bohr neighbourhood. Modern additive-combinatorics device; no counterpart in 1936.
$B$-homomorphism. Internal Gowers definition; no counterpart in Erdos-Turan.
$\gamma$-homomorphism of order $k$ (approximate-additivity). Internal to Gowers's machinery; no counterpart.
Domain / multifunction / $(B,L)$-invariance. Internal scaffolding of Gowers's structural theorem. No counterpart in Erdos-Turan.
Vertical parallelogram / $\varphi(P)$. Two-dimensional Gowers-norm device; no counterpart.
$d$-arrangement and respect by $\varphi$. Internal multi-dim parallelogram object; no counterpart.
Product property with parameter $\gamma$. Internal property in Gowers's induction; no counterpart.
Configuration / cube / parallelepiped pair / multi-dim $d$-arrangement. Internal Gowers definitions; no counterpart.
$(\gamma,r)$-multiply $k$-linear. Internal Gowers structural definition; no counterpart.
$\alpha$-uniform of degree $k$ wrt partition. Internal Gowers definition; no counterpart.
Fourth-power Fourier identity and equivalent formulations of uniformity. Building blocks of $U^2$ analysis; no counterpart in Erdos-Turan.
Fourth power as additive-quadruple count. Standard Fourier identity used by Gowers; no counterpart in 1936.
Linear-progression partition lemma and density-increment from large Fourier coefficient. Roth-style Fourier toolkit; not present in 1936.
Proof of Roth via density-increment iteration with Fourier dichotomy. Method not present in Erdos-Turan.
Equivalent formulations of higher-degree uniformity, Cauchy-Schwarz step-down, and interval intersection estimate. Higher-order Fourier analysis machinery; entirely post-Gowers.
Higher-uniformity AP-count bound, approximate AP count for uniform sets, higher uniformity implies APs. Core technical theorems of Gowers's pseudorandomness apparatus; no counterpart in 1936.
Cube-count bounds, Cauchy-Schwarz cube inequality, and the Gowers norm $\|\cdot\|_d$ itself. Defining objects of the new technique; no counterpart.
Conjecture: uniform sets have at least the expected number of 4-APs. A modern formulation specific to Gowers norms; no counterpart in Erdos-Turan.

Section 5 toolkit: Weyl/Dirichlet exponential-sum estimates, polynomial partition lemmas, mod-$N$-AP refinement, density-increment from partition. The bulk of the analytic-number-theory inputs Gowers needs; entirely post-1936.

Section 6-7 machinery: quadratic-non-uniformity to $\gamma$-additive functions, Balog-Szemeredi-Freiman cycle, Bogolyubov-style Bohr-homomorphism extraction. None of this is anticipated by Erdos-Turan.

Length-4 Szemeredi (and its proof). The first genuinely new theorem of Gowers — the special case beyond Roth where the new technique already requires its full quadratic apparatus. Not foreseen in any concrete sense in 1936.
Section 9: Hoelder fourth-power, sixteenth-power additivity, random restriction to approximate homomorphism. Internal to Gowers.

Section 10: domain / multifunction structural theorem, base point, smoothness, well-behaved subset, local difference function $\psi$ as Freiman homomorphism, Bohr-shift size estimate, induced homomorphism, approximate-homomorphism Bohr-restriction theorem. Major internal Gowers structural result. No counterpart.

Section 12: multi-function additive-quadruple bound, vertical-parallelogram counting, 8-arrangement count, random restriction. Two-dimensional analogue of Section 6/9 internal to Gowers. No counterpart.
Section 13: bilinear-piece extraction for cubic non-uniformity (the weak bilinear Freiman). Internal Gowers result; no counterpart.
Section 14: multi-function product-property machinery, respected configurations / cube pairs / parallelepiped pairs / 8-arrangements. Internal Gowers structural lemmas; no counterpart.
Section 15: Walsh-basis non-degeneracy, parity-function characterization, multilinear-fiber-size bound, degenerate-arrangement count, random restriction in multi-dim, combination lemma. Internal.

Section 16: main inductive structural theorem ($(\gamma, r)$-multiply $k$-linearity) and its proof by induction on $k$; multilinear piece corollary for $(k+1)$-uniformity failure. The technical heart of Gowers's higher-order Fourier analysis. Entirely beyond 1936.
Section 17: polynomial expansion of multilinear functions, polynomial-bias from full or boxed multilinear function, VC-dim counting of half-spaces and affine functions on $\{0,1\}^k$. Internal.
Density-increment-from-non-uniformity theorem and its proof. Internal Gowers theorem combining the multilinear piece (CP339.22) with the polynomial-bias partition (PrP339.7). No counterpart.

Proof of the Main Theorem (TP339.13) via density-increment iteration controlled by TP339.12 and CP339.4. The proof technique is the modern density-increment paradigm; Erdos-Turan use elementary subadditive induction, so the proofs of the paired main theorems share no tactical structure.

Multidimensional Szemeredi quantitative bound (corners $\{(a,b),(a+d,b),(a,b+d)\}$ in $[N]^2$). A 2D extension Gowers leaves open in his concluding remarks. Erdos-Turan 1936 do not consider multidimensional patterns at all, so no counterpart.
